chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from one of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), regarding the man who buys a garment or goods and finds a defect in it.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the item is still intact in its essence, he may return it to him and take back the price; but if the garment has been cut, or stitched, or dyed, he returns it with a deduction for the defect.'
ai.seo_question: What are the buyer's rights when a purchased item has a hidden defect?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'khiyar al-ayb' (option of defect) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between full rescission when the item is intact and partial compensation when altered. It reflects the practical application of fairness in commercial transactions, ensuring the buyer is not penalized for defects they did not cause, while protecting the seller from arbitrary returns after significant modification.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who buys the clothes or the goods, so he finds defact in it.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the thing was standing with exactness (as it used to be), he can return it to him and take the money, however, if the cloth had been cut, or stitched, or dyed, he would return it with a reduction for the defact’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil from certain persons of our people who has said the following: “I once asked one of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about the case of a man who buys cloths or goods and finds defects in it.
He (the Imam) said, ‘If the item is exactly as it was, he can return and get back what he has paid and if the cloth is cut or stitched or dyed he must pay for the loss.’”
